turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Grand so, sleeve up there and I'll get the blood pressure before the doctor.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah yeah. I'm wrecked. Can we not drag this whole thing out.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure one thirty eight over eighty four. Pulse seventy two. Temperature thirty six point six. Oxygen ninety eight percent.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm. Sure it was higher the last time.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): That's the reading for today. Doctor'll be straight in.
[SEG0006] person_3 (DOCTOR): Doctor Keane. What's the problem.
[SEG0007] person_2 (PATIENT): Uh, the room spins. A few seconds, when I turn over in the bed, or when I look up at the press.
[SEG0008] person_4 (CAREGIVER): I'm Nuala, her daughter, I stay with her. She told me it came on Thursday.
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah, Thursday. I'm well able to say it myself.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): Seconds only?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): Yeah. It stops if I lie still.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): Sick to your stomach?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): Queasy. I don't want my food.
[SEG0014] person_4 (CAREGIVER): She threw up twice yesterday. I heard her in the bathroom.
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): I did not throw up. Nothing came up, I just felt rotten. Stop adding bits.
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any hearing loss?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Ear pain?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Fever?
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cough?
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): No cough.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any change in your weight?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): I don't know. Maybe. The trousers are a bit loose, but sure I'm not eating, I couldn't give you a number.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any tablets?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm. Amladipine five milligrams in the morning. And the odd paracetamol.
[SEG0028] person_4 (CAREGIVER): Err, she doesn't take the amladipine every morning. I've seen it left sitting in the box.
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): I take it most days. Leave off.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Drug allergies?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll do a Dix-Hallpike now. Head to the right, I'll tip you back quick.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): My neck is sore from sleeping crooked. Go on, hurry up then.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Back you come. Right, positive on the right. Eyes are flicking, a short burst, then it settles.
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Ugh. That's the exact spinning. Are you finished.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Working impression is benign positional vertigo. Crystals in the inner ear, shifting when you move.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): Right. So what do I actually do.

[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do the Epley at home three times a day until it eases: sit up, turn the head, lie back, roll over, and hold each position about thirty seconds. Nuala can watch you do it. Don't drive if a spin is coming on, and I'll script prochlorperazine five milligrams up to three times a day for the nausea. If you're still spinning in two weeks, come back to me.

spec.situation: Spinning for a few seconds when turning in bed or looking up, since last week; nausea; no hearing loss, no ear pain; doctor does a positional test and teaches the exercise.

traps.happens: The doctor asks only two to four review-of-systems questions (for example fever, weight, cough). Several other body systems are never asked about. One of the asked questions gets a vague or mixed answer.
traps.label_rule: negative_findings / review_of_systems ONLY for items the doctor actually asked AND the patient answered, evidence = that question and answer. Never add review-of-systems entries for systems nobody asked about, and never cite an unrelated turn (for example a turn about tiredness) for a system review.

features: relative_speaks_for_patient: a relative answers for the patient and the patient partly contradicts; reported_by follows who said it.

spoken_numbers: doses, vitals and durations are spoken as words or sloppy speech ('a hundred and two point five', 'one-forty over ninety', 'five-ish years', 'twenty milligram'); the label writes them normally (102.5, 140/90, 20 mg) and does not turn vague ones into exact ones.

bad.reason: Amlodipine 5 mg stated, but 'every morning' is disputed; patient says most days.
bad.text: amlodipine (dose=5 mg, frequency=every morning, status=currently_used, reported_by=patient)

omissions.text: Vertigo episodes stop if she lies still.
Asked about weight change: patient unsure, says trousers are a bit loose and she cannot give a number.
Current amlodipine use is recorded inaccurately as every morning; caregiver reports missed doses and patient says she takes it most days, so adherence is inconsistent rather than every morning.
Dix-Hallpike was positive on the right.
